question_text: Find the equation of the polar of (1,−2) with respect to x² + y² − 10x − 10y + 25 = 0.

insider_note: The polar formula is the same as the tangent formula S₁ = 0 — the only difference is that the point need not be on the circle, and here it is not.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the polar formula
steps.margin_note: One mark. Halve −10 and −10 to get g = −5 and f = −5.
steps.memory_tip: Polar of P(x₁, y₁) is S₁ = xx₁ + yy₁ + g(x + x₁) + f(y + y₁) + c = 0.
lines: Polar of P(x₁, y₁) is S₁ = 0
⇒ xx₁ + yy₁ + g(x + x₁) + f(y + y₁) + c = 0
steps.why: The polar has the same form as the tangent at a point on the circle. Halving the coefficients is what turns 2g into g inside the bracket.
common_mistakes: Using −10 in place of g and f.
Writing g(x · x₁) instead of g(x + x₁).

steps.label: Substitute and simplify
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Multiply through by −1 at the end so the leading coefficient is positive.
steps.memory_tip: Collect the x terms, the y terms and the numbers separately before tidying.
steps.why: The x terms give x − 5x = −4x, the y terms give −2y − 5y = −7y and the numbers give −5 + 10 + 25 = 30. Multiplying by −1 puts the answer in its usual form.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer with a negative leading coefficient, which is correct but is usually rewritten.
